script.base: Atlanta is a 7-point home favorite in a closed roof with a moderate 44.5 total, so the book expects a lead of about a touchdown and a 25.8-18.8 game, not a shootout. The base flow is Atlanta ahead by halftime and grinding late through Bijan Robinson, who already has 50 carries and 285 rush yards in the pack's weeks 4/6/7 window (16.7 carries and 95 yards a game, 5.7 YPC), with Tyler Allgeier as the complement (30 carries, 99 yards) if his hip allows it. Miami, priced at 18.8, spends the second half throwing: Jaylen Waddle is the hub at 21 targets, 220 yards and 357 air yards in weeks 5-7, while De'Von Achane's 39 carries / 226 rush yards are the volume that shrinks if the Dolphins abandon the run.
script.flip1: Michael Penix Jr. (questionable, knee) or Drake London (questionable, hip) is limited and Miami hangs around or leads. Atlanta cannot clock-kill, so Bijan's carries slide toward the 40-yard game in his last four (72, 75, 170, 40) and the offense has to live through London, Kyle Pitts (19 targets, 150 yards, 122 air) and Bijan's receiving role (21 targets, 226 yards). Achane can stay a featured rusher, as in the 99-, 128- and 82-yard games in his last four.
script.flip2: Atlanta jumps out by two scores. Bijan and, if active, Allgeier kill the clock, and a true blowout trims Bijan's late snaps even though -7 is not an automatic sit-the-starters number. Miami's rush share dies — Ollie Gordon II already has only 10 carries for 10 yards in three weeks — and targets pile onto Waddle, with Malik Washington (18 targets) and Achane (18 targets, 7 air yards) as the checkdown answers. Atlanta's 43% blitz and Tua's -0.44 EPA per dropback versus the blitz can turn those extra attempts into empty yards rather than a Waddle ceiling game.

pre_mortem: It is Monday and both legs lost. Norton's absence blew up the run fits, Miami's pass defense (8.59 YPA to the right, 17 explosives, Marshall out) was the easier path, and a playable Allgeier took the late carries while Penix's knee kept Atlanta from ever leading by enough to grind. Bijan finished in the 40-72 band on about 12 carries. On the other side Atlanta blitzed at the season 43 percent, Walker or not, Tua's EPA cratered, and Waddle posted the 15-yard template while Achane and Washington caught the checkdowns. Bowman being out produced one shot that Hill, not Waddle, caught, which is why a Hill under was never paired with this over. The median rungs needed better-than-typical efficiency and the missing tackle plus the blitz took it.
slip_story: One script only: Atlanta leads and runs, Miami trails and throws to its WR1. Two-leg favorite-clock-kill plus dog-primary stack, no touchdowns, no second market on either player, no total under mixed with these overs, and no Achane rush leg that needs the opposite script. Hill, Washington and Waller are the same-game pass pieces that would need a checkdown script rather than Waddle's air yards, so they stay off the slip. London and Pitts overs would need Atlanta to throw through questionable tags, which fights the grind. Stake is a proposal only and is zero until a no-vig exists; nothing is placed.
